CONSUMER FINANCIAL PROTECTION BUREAU
Bureau of Consumer Financial Protection
1700 G Street, N.W., Washington, D.C. 20552

CIVIL INVESTIGATIVE DEMAND
Docket No. 2026-INV-FT-0088

To: Kinetic Ledger Payments, Inc. ("Kinetic")
    (d/b/a "PaySwift" and "SwiftPay")
    77 Oak Lawn Avenue, Suite 400
    Dallas, Texas 75207

Attention: Ford D. Halloran, General Counsel

Date: June 3, 2026

Pursuant to Section 1052 of the Consumer Financial Protection Act of 2010, 12 U.S.C. § 5562, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ("Bureau") issues this Civil Investigative Demand ("CID") to Kinetic Ledger Payments, Inc.

NOTIFICATION OF PURPOSE
The purpose of this investigation is to determine whether money-transmitter operators, payment platforms, or other persons have engaged in or are engaging in unlawful acts or practices in violation of Sections 1031 or 1036 of the CFPA (12 U.S.C. §§ 5531, 5536) — including unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices ("UDAAP") — the Electronic Fund Transfer Act (15 U.S.C. § 1693 et seq.) and Regulation E (12 C.F.R. Part 1005), or the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, in connection with peer-to-peer payment applications, transaction dispute resolution processes, error-resolution procedures, and disclosures.

DOCUMENT REQUESTS

The Bureau requests that Kinetic produce, no later than July 15, 2026, the following documents for the period January 1, 2024 through the date of this CID:

1. All policies, procedures, and training materials relating to:
   (a) Error resolution under Regulation E § 1005.11;
   (b) Investigation and adjudication of consumer claims of unauthorized transfers;
   (c) Customer service scripts for handling fraud, scam, and unauthorized transfer complaints, including any distinction the Bank draws between "unauthorized" and "authorized-but-fraudulent" transactions.

2. All aggregated data, in structured (CSV or Parquet) format, showing:
   (a) The volume of consumer error and fraud complaints received, categorized by dispute type;
   (b) The number and percentage of such complaints resolved in the consumer's favor;
   (c) The average time to provisional credit and to final resolution;
   (d) Complaints escalated to the Better Business Bureau, state attorneys general, or the Bureau's Consumer Complaint Database.

3. All internal communications, including electronic mail and Slack messages, of Chief Product Officer Yasmin R. Kettering and Vice President of Risk Operations Callum J. Bright referring to:
   (a) "Zelle-like scams" or "authorized push payment fraud";
   (b) The July 24, 2025 New York Times article titled "P2P Payments' Fraud Problem";
   (c) The Bureau's June 15, 2023 Circular 2023-02 concerning liability for unauthorized transfers.

4. All internal audits and third-party assessments relating to the operation of the SwiftPay peer-to-peer transfer service.

5. A list of all state money-transmitter licenses currently held by Kinetic and copies of all state examination reports issued to Kinetic since January 1, 2023.

6. All consumer complaints received by Kinetic regarding scams commonly known as (a) romance scams, (b) impersonation scams (bank impersonators, government impersonators), (c) marketplace/purchase scams, and (d) investment/crypto scams.

INTERROGATORIES

7. Describe in detail how Kinetic distinguishes between "unauthorized" transactions (as defined in 12 C.F.R. § 1005.2(m)) and other categories of disputed transactions. Identify by title all personnel who make these determinations and their training.

8. Provide the total dollar amount of consumer losses reported to Kinetic through SwiftPay disputes in each calendar year 2024 and 2025, disaggregated by transaction type.

9. Describe all changes made to the SwiftPay user interface in the last 24 months relating to fraud warnings, confirmation screens, or transaction reversibility.

MEET AND CONFER
The Bureau's counsel of record, Attorney Yolanda C. Prevost (yolanda.prevost@cfpb.gov), is available to meet and confer regarding the scope and modality of production. Please contact Attorney Prevost within 10 days of receipt.

CONFIDENTIALITY
Information provided in response to this CID may be treated as confidential pursuant to 12 C.F.R. § 1070.41(c).

/s/ Rebecca Sagawa, Deputy Enforcement Director
CONSUMER FINANCIAL PROTECTION BUREAU
